comments.body:
Dogfooding finding (self-verification of this story's own changes caught a real defect in an earlier iteration):

1. **Primary-banks-nothing defect** — the reworked primary run had the `record_criterion_verdict` tool + banking prompt but was never told the minted criterion IDs (only successors received them). Fixed by injecting a `primary_criteria_manifest()` (id -> truncated text) into the primary's ticket_context via a new `extra_context` seam on RunnerAgentStep. Confirmed necessary + sufficient: with the manifest, the primary banks (14/19 under induced exhaustion); without it, 0.

2. **Banking-prompt judgment regression (caught by AC "healthy-path quality")** — a first prompt rewrite that forced STRICT one-criterion-at-a-time verification ("gather only that criterion's evidence, do not read ahead, bank, then advance") DEGRADED verdict quality: closed ticket 003d-e6b0 verified PASS under the committed prompt but FAIL under the strict prompt (both 0 budget hits; identical code state). Root cause: forbidding holistic exploration starved the model's cross-criterion judgment. The flip localized to an execution-only criterion ("`make test` green") that is inherently unverifiable from static analysis. Reverted to a BALANCED prompt: keeps "bank each verdict the moment you're confident, don't batch at the end" (which alone drives strong incremental banking — 14/19) but removes the strict-isolation / no-read-ahead framing. Post-fix healthy-path re-verify: f6fc, 01f8, 02e9 all PASS.

Observability added: completion_recovery logs `primary banked N of M criteria before exhaustion` at the primary->recovery handoff (the K in K-of-N survival).

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

The shipped completion-recovery design fans out one ISOLATED evidence run per criterion after a primary-run failure. The operator has ruled this an unapproved design overreach: it explodes token cost (c9f7 shape: 22 criteria x 20-request budget = 440 requests worst case, 1.8x the primary's own 240-request budget) and wall-clock cost (sequential 25-90s per criterion), re-sends the full ticket context uncached per criterion (2.67M chars for c9f7), and has no optimization for overlapping or small criteria. Meanwhile verified work from the PRIMARY run is discarded wholesale when it fails: a run that verified 20 of 22 criteria before exhausting re-does everything. And when recovery itself dies, the run ends verdict-less — the --force-close trap.

## Approach

Replace the per-criterion fan-out (completion_recovery.py _recover, deleted not dead-coded) with banked incremental verification at the CompletionAgentStep seam (completion_recovery.py:451+). All numbered evidence below was confirmed by reading the tree at the cited lines.

**Criterion identity.** Deterministic ID minted at run start: `c<two-digit index>-<sha256(normalized verbatim text)[:8]>` (normalization: whitespace-collapse + casefold). explicit_completion_criteria (completion_recovery.py:84) is a deterministic, deduped, document-order parse, so primary and successor mint identical IDs from the same material. Bank entries carry BOTH the id and the verbatim string; the final completion_verdict still keys by verbatim string (schema unchanged). The id keys the bank, the record tool's schema, the successor prompt's remainder listing, and a reworked coverage validation that accepts the banked-union-successor set by ID, order-insensitive (today's _validate_coverage, completion_recovery.py:354, requires ordered full-list equality and cannot accept a remainder-scoped result; its retry-on-missing behavior is preserved).

**Run-scoped bank.** Lives in a run-unique git-ignored dir `.rebar/workflow_runs/<run_id>/bank/` (run_id exists, workflow/executor.py:71), so concurrent closes cannot collide; no cross-run reuse — the staleness surface is too large for a signed gate. Fail-loud (any read/write error aborts recovery with a typed error), schema-versioned, idempotent upsert by criterion_id. Each entry stamps ticket id, ticket-material fingerprint (the same provenance seam _commands/transition_close.py already imports), and the resolved verification tree sha (for a --ref close, the resolved ref's tree — the same tree the signature retargets to, _lib_writes.py:370). The successor preflight re-resolves all three stamps and fails loud on any mismatch. The bank dir is discarded after finalize; the emitted verdict/sidecar embeds the banked evidence uncompressed so the audit trail survives it.

**Primary run.** Gains a `record_criterion_verdict` tool wired through a new explicit constructor/step-input seam on CompletionAgentStep feeding RunRequest.extra_tools (the dormant field built for this; runner.py:347-348 appends it — the primary RunRequest is built inside RunnerAgentStep.run, workflow/runs.py:144). The system prompt (reviewers/completion_verifier.md) instructs INCREMENTAL banking — record each criterion's verdict as soon as its evidence is sufficient — and states that banked verdicts are PROVISIONAL AND REVISABLE (re-recording overwrites; the idempotent upsert supports it), with the final structured output remaining the authoritative full-list judgment on success. This reconciles mid-run banking with the batched-judging research's reason-across-all-criteria-before-committing recommendation. Each banked entry's evidence is capped at banking time at 3,000 chars (sized net of finalizer prompt overhead and criteria text: _MAX_FINALIZER_INPUT_CHARS = 132,000 (completion_recovery.py:70) minus _MAX_TOTAL_CRITERIA_CHARS = 32,000 and prompt overhead, divided by _MAX_CRITERIA = 32 (completion_recovery.py:41)); a capped entry carries an explicit truncated=true flag — the audit trail declares partial evidence rather than leaving it discoverable only by measuring lengths (this cap deliberately replaces the oversize-evidence fail-loud at completion_recovery.py:346-351). The cap is enforced by the tool and stated to the model. Precedence: on primary SUCCESS the final structured output is authoritative exactly as today; the bank is consulted ONLY on typed failure — no behavior change for healthy runs.

**Successor runs.** On typed primary failure (LLMBudgetExhausted | RunawayToolLoop | token-exhaustion UnretryableOutput — the three CompletionAgentStep already catches): batched successor runs over the UNVERIFIED remainder.
- Batch cap keys on the RESOLVED verifier class SLOT, using the real model_classes.py vocabulary trivial/standard/frontier (there is no "Sonnet-class"): standard (the default verifier slot, VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL, model_classes.py:55) => <=8 criteria/batch, frontier (model_classes.py:54) => <=12, trivial => <=8. The slot is resolved by matching the verifier's resolved model against the class-slot models via load_class_slots / SLOT defaults (model_classes.py:47-56, 133-141); an unrecognized model falls back to the standard cap of 8. Research ground: FARA-style whole-rubric 12-15 is frontier-only, mid-tier caps at 6-8.
- Runs = ceil(remainder/cap), sequential, each ONE batched agentic run — never per-criterion. Worst case today: 22 remainder on Sonnet -> 3 runs.
- Successors carry the SAME record_criterion_verdict tool and incremental-banking instruction: a successor dying mid-run in a typed failure keeps its banked progress; only still-unbanked criteria count as no-progress. On successor success its structured output is harvested into the bank via the same idempotent upsert (tool-banked and output-harvested entries converge; re-harvest is a no-op).
- BUDGET POOL, denominated in MODEL REQUESTS. N = the primary's req_limit as computed by build_usage_limits (structured_run.py:452: req_limit = ceil(eff_max_iter/2)); with lever 1 completion floors eff_max_iter at the criteria-scaled verify_step_floor(c) (replacing the flat 480), so N = ceil(verify_step_floor(c)/2) — for f6fc (c=8) floor=clamp(64,48,480)=64 => N=32; the c>=60 clamp-max case is N=240 as before. Global total = completion_recovery_pool_multiplier x N (new config key, default 1.5); successor pool = global - primary spend (from the typed failure's failure_usage.requests diagnostic, structured_run.py:84-137), so a fully-exhausted primary leaves 0.5 x N (f6fc: 16; clamp-max: 120). Honest empirical anchor: the only whole-ticket instrumented datum (the non-looping instrumented run: 14 criteria, 258 tool calls, 238 distinct) DIED budget-exhausted verdict-less, as did all four instrumented runs at 257-270 calls — that shows whole-ticket verification can consume a full primary budget; it does not show the successor pool suffices. The sufficiency argument is structural: successor batches carry <=8 criteria not the full list; banked verdicts arrive as one-line read-only summaries so completed work is not re-verified; and the failure mode when the pool is exhausted is benign by construction — the run degrades to a full-coverage verdict with unverified met=false placeholders, a scored outcome, never the trap. The 1.5 default is an economics dial (config-tunable); unit tests pin the arithmetic as a function of c against the true numbers (f6fc c=8: N=32, pool=48, successor pool=16; clamp-max c>=60: N=240, pool=360, successor pool=120).
- Per-run allocation: each of the R planned runs gets floor(pool_remaining / runs_remaining) — run 1 cannot drain runs 2..R; later runs inherit unspent budget. Success-path spend seam: pydantic-ai run usage is already extracted post-run (runner.py:538); this ticket returns it to CompletionAgentStep on the run result so inheritance sees actual successor spend.
- Unit conversion at the seam: iteration_limit is in ITERATIONS and build_usage_limits derives req_limit = ceil(eff_max_iter/2), so a successor granted B requests sets iteration_limit = 2 x B (passing B raw would silently halve every successor budget). B > N clamps at N: iteration_limit is min-only against cfg.max_iterations (structured_run.py:447-448), so allocation is capped at N per run.
- No-launch guard, batch-aware: a batch of k criteria needs >= 2k tool calls (>=1 read + 1 bank each) and tool_calls_limit = max(8, 2xB) (structured_run.py:455), so the launch floor is B >= 2 x batch_size. Below it, shrink the batch to floor(B/2) and re-plan (re-computing the per-run allocation after each shrink; terminates — batch size strictly decreases); when even a 1-criterion batch (B < 2) cannot launch, stop and finalize with what is banked (the max(2,·) floor at structured_run.py:448 would otherwise grant a doomed 1-request run at pool 0).
- Scoping: remainder criteria listed by ID; banked verdicts as read-only one-line summaries; FULL ticket context unchanged (no elision). Deliberate deviation from pydantic-ai message_history resume: a clean-scoped successor avoids resuming a history that just looped 144x (poisoned attention); the re-paid context cost is accepted and mitigated by the cache note below.
- Structured output: required per-criterion fields keyed by ID + retry-on-missing (the _validate_coverage retry precedent).
- Zero-progress breaker: a successor banking nothing new (neither tool nor harvest) stops recovery; control passes to the finalizer with whatever the bank holds.

**Finalizer & verdict coverage** (existing tool-free finalizer, completion_recovery.py:545+):
- If ANY verdicts are banked, it ALWAYS emits a FULL-COVERAGE verdict: verified criteria scored from banked evidence; unverified criteria as met=false placeholders explicitly marked exhausted/unverified (content-free counters only). The deterministic backstop guarantees an exhausted placeholder can never score met=true. The verdict-less --force-close trap is closed for every state with progress.
- Deterministic no-LLM fallback: if the LLM finalizer itself fails, retry it once; if it fails again, assemble the verdict DIRECTLY from the bank with no model call — banked met flags as-is, unbanked criteria as met=false unverified placeholders, downgrade authority skipped and recorded as skipped. A run with banked progress can NEVER die verdict-less. The fallback verdict closes the ticket but is stamped finalizer=deterministic_fallback and, in the SAME emitted verdict, sets certifiable=false — the field completion_sidecar records at completion_sidecar.py:290 and that the signing path already reads to withhold a certified signature. This is the ticket's OWN self-verdict provenance, DISTINCT from child_closure_findings (completion.py:90-193), which drives certifiable=false only from unattested CHILD signatures; deterministic_fallback withholds certification of this ticket's own close because its cross-criterion downgrade review never ran. The upgrade path is the existing reopen -> re-close flow.
- Downgrade authority over banked PASSes on cross-criterion contradiction (banked-PASS revision is unsolved community-wide; this is the mitigation).
- Receives uncompressed evidence (byte-identity pinned, subject only to the banking-time per-entry cap with its truncated flag).
- The ONE remaining verdict-less state — zero banked verdicts total — stays a typed CompletionRecoveryError + gate_error sidecar, deliberately: an all-placeholder FAIL would conflate not-done with not-verified on a signed gate; zero progress signals pathology needing diagnosis. The incremental-banking live AC below is what makes this state rare.

**Cache.** The shared cache is the EXISTING automatic prompt-cache, not a new inline CachePoint. Two arms of cache_settings_for (capabilities.py:679-701) apply: (a) cache_instructions + cache_tool_definitions are unconditionally on, so the system prompt (reviewers/completion_verifier.md) and the tool-definition block are cached breakpoints; (b) the message-tail arm sets anthropic_cache / bedrock_cache_messages only when execution_mode in _MESSAGE_TAIL_EXECUTION_MODES (the agentic verifier qualifies), placing the third breakpoint at the message-tail END — the provider-managed prefix cache, NOT a hand-placed CachePoint after the ticket block. Because each successor re-sends a byte-identical system-prompt + tool-definition prefix (the ticket context is unchanged; only the remainder-criteria/banked-summary tail differs), arms (a) always hit primary->successor; the tail arm (b) caches each run's own tail for its internal turns. The live exhaustion AC measures this reuse from the successor's usage log (cache-read tokens > 0).

**Primary step floor — criteria-scaled (lever 1).** The shipped flat floor `_VERIFY_MIN_STEPS = 480` (completion.py:86) is the root cause of most recoveries, not merely a safety ceiling. Instrumented confirmation (docs/experiments/diag_runaway_matrix.py + diag-runaway-transcript.md, recorded on the discovered-work ticket d2df linked below): the SAME f6fc (8-criteria) verification, greedy decoding, same tree, run at three step floors — floor 50 (25 req) converged to a clean PASS at ~100 tool calls and tripped the runaway guard in 0/3 runs; floor 240 (120 req) tripped 2/2; floor 480 (240 req) tripped 3/3. The verifier reaches sufficient evidence around ~100 tool calls / 25 requests but does NOT stop when handed more budget — the surplus is spent on the measured 77%-re-read waste the runaway guard then correctly catches. The flat floor thus hands an 8-criteria ticket ~10x the budget it needs and MANUFACTURES the exhaustion banking then has to recover from. This ticket replaces the flat floor with a criteria-scaled one: `verify_step_floor(c) = clamp(completion_verify_steps_per_criterion x c, completion_verify_step_floor_min, 480)` where c = len(explicit_completion_criteria); defaults `verify_steps_per_criterion = 8`, `verify_step_floor_min = 48` (both new config keys). It stays min-only against an explicit operator budget exactly as the flat floor is today (an explicit higher REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS still wins), and the old flat 480 is retained as the clamp MAX so no ticket ever exceeds today's ceiling. This makes typical tickets converge WITHOUT entering recovery — attacking the runaway at its source — while the banking net above still catches the genuinely large ticket that exhausts even its scaled budget. Scope provenance: lever 1 (and lever 2) is discovered work surfaced by this epic's own instrumentation (ticket d2df, linked discovered_from this story), folded into 2948 under explicit operator approval; it is in-scope for 10ae because it directly reduces the recovery load this epic reworks — the two levers cut the frequency at which the banking net is exercised at all.

**Read-file memo normalization (lever 2).** The f6fc memo (agent_call.py MEMO_ALLOWLIST) keys on the exact tool signature INCLUDING read_file's line_start/line_end, so the measured re-read waste — 48 read_file calls hitting only 11 distinct files, 77% re-reads (same diagnostic) — slips past it because re-reads use different ranges. This ticket normalizes the read_file memo key by PATH: on the first read of a path the memo caches the file's WHOLE content (the line_start=1, line_end=0 form read_file already supports) and serves EVERY subsequent read of that path — any range — by slicing the cached content, re-executing only under the f6fc error rule (an "Error:"-prefixed whole-file read is not cached, so a transient failure re-executes). Repeats still carry the graduated nudge. This collapses the dominant re-read tax during verification; it is confined to read_file (the other allowlisted tools keep exact-signature memoization) and preserves read_file's "(empty range)" sentinel for out-of-range slices, computed deterministically from the cache. (Note the interaction with lever 1: a smaller primary budget plus a re-read-collapsing memo compound — fewer wasted calls AND less room to waste them.)

## Scope

- src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py — delete the per-criterion fan-out; criterion IDs; successor batching + budget pool; finalizer full-coverage + deterministic fallback; reworked coverage validation.
- src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_banking.py — new: run-scoped bank store + record_criterion_verdict tool (stamps, caps, idempotent upsert, truncated flag).
- src/rebar/llm/workflow/runs.py — constructor/step-input seam passing the per-run toolset into RunRequest.extra_tools.
- src/rebar/llm/runner.py — return extracted run usage on the run result (success-path spend seam).
- src/rebar/llm/completion.py — replace the flat _VERIFY_MIN_STEPS floor with the criteria-scaled verify_step_floor(c) (lever 1). _VERIFY_MIN_STEPS is defined at completion.py:86 and applied at 523-524; both are replaced. Reference inventory for the removed symbol (Serena find_referencing_symbols + grep for the string): tests/interfaces/contracts/test_completion_budget.py imports it (line 21) and asserts `_VERIFY_MIN_STEPS == 480` (49) and `max_iterations == _VERIFY_MIN_STEPS` (55) — this contract test is UPDATED in the same change to assert the criteria-scaled floor instead; operations.py:36 is a comment-only mention of the pattern and is left as-is (the review verb keeps its own lighter floor).
- src/rebar/llm/agent_call.py — normalize the read_file memo key by path: whole-file cache + range slice (lever 2).
- src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md — incremental provisional banking instruction.
- src/rebar/_config_schema.py — three new FLAT fields on VerifyConfig matching the existing completion_* convention (alongside completion_priority_floor:236, completion_preserve_criteria:241, completion_floor_active:246): completion_recovery_pool_multiplier: float = 1.5, completion_verify_steps_per_criterion: int = 8, completion_verify_step_floor_min: int = 48. These are flat dataclass fields, NOT a new dotted completion.* config section.
- tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_banking.py — new: bank semantics, pool arithmetic (as a function of c), coverage merge, fallback.
- tests/unit/test_agent_call_memo_nudge.py — extend: read_file path-normalized memo (lever 2).
- tests/interfaces/contracts/test_completion_budget.py — update the _VERIFY_MIN_STEPS contract assertions to the criteria-scaled floor (see the completion.py entry above).
- The _recover fan-out entry point (completion_recovery.py:552, dispatched from :541/:546/:550) is the code being reworked in-place: its per-criterion body is deleted and replaced by successor batching; the three dispatch call sites remain but now invoke the batched recovery.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] K-of-N survival: with K banked verdicts and a typed primary failure, the emitted verdict scores those K from banked evidence and the remaining N-K are covered by successors or explicit met=false unverified placeholders — full coverage, never verdict-less (unit tests).
- [ ] Remainder scoping: successor prompts list only unbanked criterion IDs; banked criteria appear only as one-line read-only summaries (unit test on prompt assembly).
- [ ] Coverage-merge validates the banked-union-successor set by criterion ID, order-insensitive, retry-on-missing preserved (unit tests).
